M1.published_boundary2_text: This registry is the authority at THREE boundaries, not one. (1) Grammar-bundle admission: a row's declared syntaxClass must equal the registered one, in both directions. (2) Every admitted fact2 under a syntax universe: every ANCHOR PATH must be read by a SELECTED grammar whose capability set contains that relation@rung. (3) Every requested subject-scope under a syntax universe, INCLUDING an empty view: judged on the committed examined extent, where a code capability needs at least one extent path read by a selected code grammar, and a capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable. INVENTORY CAPABILITIES (file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared, vcs-change@vcs-reported) are ALWAYS available and are never grammar-gated at boundary (2) OR boundary (3). An earlier revision stated that exemption only inside boundary (3), and boundary (2) read as an unconditional every-anchor rule; a literal implementer therefore refused the very inventory facts boundary (3) had just promised were unconditionally available, which made an inventoried .py path inventoriable and unrepresentable at the same time. The exemption belongs to both because it is a property of the RELATION, not of the boundary: an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all - it is the snapshot inventory row, the manifest declaration or the VCS observation - so there is no grammar for it to be gated on. Independently of this exemption the relation registry anchorLaw closes the inventory class at ZERO anchors, so an inventory fact names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test in the first place; the two laws agree and neither depends on the other. An earlier revision enforced only (1), which constrains what a bundle says about itself and not what a Run claims: Markdown declares facts, complete empty declares/clones Coverage and references@resolved-binding under resolutionAttempted=false all admitted. None of the three consults a claimed coverage value, a caller-declared class, or whether facts exist.
